_what: A manual hunt, outside the three collector arms. NOT sweep results.
_why_separate: Every row here was fetched by hand with `bdata scrape`, one URL at a time, from markets no collector covers. They are not adjudicated sweep output, they do not appear in `rows`, and they do not touch `survival`, `border_escape` or any arm. Mixing a hand-found row into a collector result would be the single most dishonest thing this project could do, so the two are kept in different files and rendered in different sections.
_why_it_exists: The three arms adjudicated every listing they returned, across 207 notices, and reached zero RED. That is either an absence or a blind spot, and the two look identical from inside the sweep. This is the test that separates them: search markets the arms never covered, by hand, and see whether the products are there.
_method: bdata scrape <url> --format markdown, then the fetched page text run through collector/normalize.py classify(), the same adjudicator the sweep uses. No rule was relaxed. Verdicts below are the code's.
_result: One RED, adjudicated by the sweep's own classifier over a committed page. A second row the classifier also called RED, held down to AMBER by hand because the recall is scoped to a date code the listing cannot show. Two further live listings at AMBER. The zero was a coverage artifact, not an absence.

findings.hazard: The front tube can fold down unexpectedly while the scooter is in use.
findings.market_note: A US closeout retailer. No collector arm covers it.
findings.page_excerpt: Acer ES Series 3 Electric Scooter - AES015 | Your Price: $379.99 | Add to Cart | Availability: Item is in stock | Condition: New | Brand: Acer
findings.why_it_holds: CPSC scopes this recall by model alone, roughly 510 units, sold through February 2026, with no serial number or date-code qualifier. The model string is on the page, the brand is on the page, the buy control is live, and the word recall does not appear anywhere on it. There is no caveat to state.

findings.product: Maxi-Cosi FamilyFix Slide Pro ISOFIX base
findings.hazard: The indicator can show the base as correctly fitted when the child seat is not attached.
findings.market_note: A French baby-goods retailer. No collector arm covers France.
findings.caveat: Our own adjudicator cannot score this, and that is the finding rather than an excuse. buy_control_present() matches buy labels per arm, and the DE arm expects German wording. `Ajouter au panier` is French. We have no French arm, so classify() returns AMBER with reason `identifier re-asserted but no active buy control at capture time`, on a page that plainly has one. The rule was not widened to catch it. Dorel also scopes this recall to bases produced 20 Aug 2025 to 24 Mar 2026 and the listing discloses no production date, which is a second reason it is not RED.
findings.why_it_matters: It is a child car seat base whose defect is that it reports itself correctly fitted when it is not. Which is, precisely, the failure mode this entire project exists to refuse.

findings.hazard: An interior connection can overheat, posing a fire hazard.
findings.caveat: The adjudicator returns RED on this page: the model string re-asserts 29 times, the brand agrees, and `Add to Cart` is live with 1 in stock. We publish AMBER anyway. Siemens scopes the recall to units manufactured 1 Aug 2021 to 31 Aug 2022, identified by a date stamp on an internal label that no listing can show. The seller says `New-Surplus Original Box` and `may be of older version, date codes, or design`, which is consistent with the recall window and is not proof of it. Consistent is not confirmed, so the finding is held down by hand. This is the only row where our judgement is more conservative than our code, and it is recorded rather than resolved quietly, because a wall that silently overrides its own adjudicator is worth nothing.

findings.hazard: Inadequate cable cross-section and accessible live parts.
findings.market_note: A Polish welding retailer. No collector arm covers Poland.
findings.caveat: The buy control is only visible in the raw HTML, not the rendered markdown, so it required a second fetch to confirm. Two strings on the page suggesting unavailability were checked and both sit inside hidden elements or JavaScript templates rather than rendered state. The verdict is held at AMBER because it was confirmed by reading markup rather than by the adjudicator seeing a rendered control.

what_this_establishes: The three collector arms cover amazon.com, kaufland.de and flipkart.com. They adjudicated every listing they returned and confirmed nothing. One afternoon of hand searching, in markets those arms do not cover, found a recalled scooter on sale, a recalled child car seat base on sale, and two more live listings with stated caveats. The sweep's zero is therefore a statement about where we looked, not about what exists.
what_this_does_not_establish: Nothing here changes the sweep. Survival remains 0 of 180 with its interval, because that figure describes the three arms and these rows are not from the three arms. A hand-found row has weaker provenance than an adjudicated one: it was chosen by a human who was looking for it, so it carries selection bias a systematic sweep does not, and it cannot be used to estimate any rate.
the_honest_sentence: We looked in three marketplaces and found nothing. We looked in a fourth and found it in an afternoon. The distance between those two sentences is the whole problem with checking whether recalls work.
_provenance: Every fetched_at below is the modification time of the committed artifact holding that fetch, not a time typed from memory. The raw pages are in data/hunt/ so any verdict here can be re-derived by running collector/normalize.py classify() over them without re-fetching.
_verdict_fields: code_verdict is what collector/normalize.py classify() returns when run over the committed page, re-derived by data/hunt/rederive.py on every run. published_verdict is what we are willing to assert. They differ on CPSC 24346 only, where the code says RED and we publish AMBER. The downgrade is conservative and is shown on the wall.
